solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique, linked answer split by the grid); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Food feature of motorway service stations, primarily sandwiches

indicators.note: to sandwich is to hold something between two outer layers, so the pair of letters goes round the middle piece
primarily asks for the first letters of the two words before it

parts.note: traffic cones are a familiar sight on motorways during roadworks

explanation.surface: A traveller notes what food is on offer at motorway service stations, mainly sandwiches.
explanation.walkthrough: The initial letters of 'service stations' give S and S, and they sandwich CONE. 'Food' looks like part of the motorway picture but is the definition on its own.
explanation.definitionFit: Scones are small baked cakes, a kind of food served with jam and cream.

clue.text: Member to stand up conspicuously

definitions.meaning: a vulgar term for the penis, here the slang word for it
to raise or tilt upright, as a dog lifts its ears or a hat is tilted jauntily

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are standard: a slang word for the male organ, and a verb for raising something upright, like ears.

clue.text: Piss myself

definitions.meaning: a childish euphemism for urinating, as opposed to number two
a colloquial way of referring to oneself, as in looking after one's own interests

explanation.definitionFit: Childish slang for a wee, and an idiom for oneself, as in 'looking out for number one'.

clue.text: Subject to debate in quiet flat

indicators.note: in places the debatable piece inside the letters for quiet

parts.note: SH is the sound made to ask for quiet
a moot point is one open to argument

explanation.surface: A matter being argued over in a hushed apartment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flat' is read as a home in the surface, but it is the adjective meaning level.
explanation.definitionFit: A flat surface is even and level, with no bumps, just as a smooth one is.

clue.text: Cheerfully at home, say turning to friend

indicators.note: turning says the two short pieces before it are read backwards together

parts.note: IN means at home, as in staying in
EG, for example, is signalled by say
an ally is a friend or supporter

explanation.surface: Someone at home, cheerfully turning to a friend for a chat.
explanation.definitionFit: Both describe acting in a warm, good-humoured, friendly manner.

clue.text: I also imagined that gent left a skidmark in the pants, one admitted

indicators.note: admitted means let in, so the numeral piece goes inside the jumble
pants as British slang for rubbish signals that the letters are a mess to be reordered

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A crude joke about a man soiling his underwear, with one person owning up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pants' looks like underwear but is the anagram signal (British slang for rubbish). Rearrange GENT, L, A, SKIDMARK, IN THE, then let I in.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb is said when two people have the same idea at once, so it means I thought so too.

clue.text: Bird to sit on head first

indicators.note: first puts the piece for head ahead of the sitting piece

parts.note: nut is slang for the head
a bird hatches eggs by sitting on them

explanation.surface: An instruction to sit on someone's head before anything else.
explanation.definitionFit: The nuthatch is a small woodland songbird that climbs tree trunks head down.

clue.text: See 5
Places to go in city — changes to parts

parts.note: LA, Los Angeles, is the usual crossword city

indicators.note: parts means splits apart, so the small word goes into the middle of the changing piece

parts.note: varies means changes
taken as written

explanation.surface: Somewhere in a city, alterations being made to parts of something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Places to go' is a euphemism, a polite phrase for toilets.
explanation.definitionFit: Where one goes when nature calls: a jokey euphemism for public toilets.

clue.text: Discharge school master before gossip

indicators.note: before puts the school and master pieces ahead of the discharge

parts.note: M is short for master, as in an MA
to ooze is to discharge slowly, as from a wound

explanation.surface: A school head is sacked before rumours spread.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Discharge' reads as dismiss; it is the oozing kind.
explanation.definitionFit: To chat in a cosy, ingratiating way, a near synonym for idle chatter or gossip.

clue.text: Appropriate birth, i.e. ventouse extraction

indicators.note: extraction says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A medical note on a birth assisted by ventouse, a suction cup used to deliver the baby.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Appropriate' looks like the adjective 'suitable'; it is the verb meaning take. A ventouse is a suction device used in childbirth.
explanation.definitionFit: To appropriate is to take something for oneself without permission, which is stealing.

clue.text: Dealers in houses after drug, mess with plants?

parts.note: E is short for ecstasy
a state is a mess, as in 'what a state'
a plant is a spy placed undercover, so plants are agents

explanation.surface: House dealers on drugs, making a mess with their pot plants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plants' looks like greenery but means spies. 'after' just links the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: These professionals buy and sell property on behalf of clients, so they deal in homes.

clue.text: Model won't listen to Hollywood

indicators.note: to model is to shape, so the letters of the phrase are reshaped

explanation.surface: A model who refuses to listen to Hollywood's advice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Model' reads as a person; it is the verb to shape.
explanation.definitionFit: A nickname for the film industry, mocking its showy, glittery glamour.

clue.text: Heavy drinker to lose everything?

definitions.meaning: an alcoholic, especially one living rough
read cryptically as win nothing, with O standing for zero

explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is cryptic: losing everything is winning nought, WIN plus O, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A slang term for an alcoholic who drinks cheap wine heavily.

clue.text: Immigrants are, we hear, consumed by wages

indicators.note: consumed by means eaten up inside, so the sounded letter goes into the wages piece

parts.note: incomes are earnings or wages

indicators.note: we hear says the clue word is to be taken as it sounds

parts.note: the word are is pronounced like the letter R

explanation.surface: A complaint that newcomers are swallowed up by the wage bill.
explanation.definitionFit: Incomers are people who have moved into an area from elsewhere, newcomers or settlers.

clue.text: Controlled teenagers from '60s and '50s with period inside

indicators.note: inside places the period piece within the two youth pieces

parts.note: mods were 1960s scooter-riding youths in Britain
teds, Teddy boys, were 1950s British youths in Edwardian-style dress
an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: Restrained youths of two past decades, with something extra inside.
explanation.walkthrough: Mods and Teddy boys were British youth subcultures of the 1960s and 1950s; one phrase supplies both groups, and the period splits them.
explanation.definitionFit: To moderate something is to keep it in check, so a moderated debate is one kept under control.

clue.text: Play around with a semi? No, drunk

indicators.note: drunk means reeling and disordered, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Fooling about with a semi-detached house? No, just drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: W (with) leads the anagram of A SEMI NO.
explanation.definitionFit: To play around is to have casual affairs, as a womaniser does with many partners.

clue.text: Like star on a drug

parts.note: a steroid is a drug, as used by athletes to build muscle

explanation.surface: A celebrity seems to be on performance-enhancing drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: Used as an adjective, the answer means star-shaped; 'Like star' reads as a celebrity comparison.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective the word means star-shaped or resembling a star, from Greek for star-like.

clue.text: Stop model making food

parts.note: to die is to stop, as an engine does
the Model T was Ford's famous car

explanation.surface: Someone's urge to stop a model from eating.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a model not eating; the Model T is Ford's early car.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone's diet is what they habitually eat, their regular food and drink.

clue.text: Cash in on diamonds, essentially need money

parts.note: RE means on or concerning, as in letters
D is the card-suit abbreviation for diamonds

indicators.note: essentially points to the heart of the word, its middle letters

parts.note: M stands for money, as in M1 money supply

explanation.surface: Someone cashing in diamonds because they badly need money.
explanation.definitionFit: To redeem a voucher or bond is to exchange it for cash or goods.

clue.text: Ultimately, large plant here as in arrangement?

definitions.text: Ultimately, large plant here as in arrangement?

indicators.note: ultimately asks for the final letter of the following word
in arrangement says the letters of the phrase are rearranged

explanation.surface: A large plant placed in a flower arrangement.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines too: a large-leaved plant used in arrangements. 'Ultimately' gives E from 'large'.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a large-leaved plant, often used as a showy foliage plant in displays.

clue.text: Small model entertaining group

indicators.note: entertaining means taking in as a guest, so the small letter goes inside

parts.note: to pose is to model, as for an artist
S is the clothing-size abbreviation for small

explanation.surface: A petite model amusing a group of people.
explanation.definitionFit: A posse is a band of people, originally one gathered by a sheriff.

clue.text: Potent man mostly learning

indicators.note: mostly says the word loses its final letter

parts.note: study is learning

explanation.surface: A virile man whose mind is mostly on learning.
explanation.definitionFit: A stud is a sexually virile man, from the breeding stallion.

clue.text: Tea in pot? Irish singer spoke endlessly

indicators.note: endlessly applies to both words, each losing its last letter

parts.note: Bono is the lead singer of the Irish band U2
said means spoke

explanation.surface: Bono talks on and on about making tea in a pot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tea' is a tea tree, grown in a pot, hence the question mark. 'endlessly' cuts the last letter from both BONO and SAID.
explanation.definitionFit: A bonsai is a miniature tree grown in a container; tea-tree is a kind of shrub.

clue.text: Name of institute with books to get into God

indicators.note: to get into means to enter, so the books piece goes inside the god

parts.note: a deity is a god
NT, the New Testament, is a set of books

explanation.surface: The name of an institute whose books are getting religion.
explanation.definitionFit: One's identity is who one is, which a name stands for.

clue.text: Without thinking, idiot finishes joint

indicators.note: finishes says the idiot piece comes at the end, after the joint

parts.note: the knee is a joint of the leg
a jerk is a fool or idiot

explanation.surface: A fool finishing off a joint of meat, or a spliff.
explanation.definitionFit: A reflexive, automatic response is made without thought, like the reflex tap on the knee.

clue.text: Managed crazy European party

parts.note: mad means crazy
a do is a party

explanation.surface: A wild party thrown by someone from Europe.
explanation.definitionFit: To make do is to cope or get by with what is available, so managed.
